newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Oct 29.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:
- A U.S. mediator pulling out of negotiations to get Israel out of the West Bank city of Hebron has revealed how peace politics in the Middle East are worsening.

- U.S. Commerce Department documents reveal how John Huang attended government meetings during which trade issues with Indonesia were discussed. Huang, a former employee of an Indonesian billionaire, worked as a trade official in President Bill Clinton's administration.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton said the country's federal deficit had dropped to its lowest level since 1981.

- Speaking against affirmative action programs, Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole said the government should only protect people from explicit discrimination and provide assistance based on economic status, not race or sex.
- John Sweeney celebrated his first year as president of the U.S. labor organization AFL-CIO.
